title: This EV Battery Has No Lithium. It Works at -40 Degrees #shorts

scenes.text: Almost every electric car runs on lithium. This battery runs on sodium, the stuff in table salt.
Sodium is about a thousand times more common in Earth's crust than lithium, and it can even come from seawater. That could make batteries much cheaper.
Now the surprise. CATL says its new Naxtra cells keep over ninety percent of their capacity at minus forty, where Celsius and Fahrenheit meet.
And at minus thirty, nearly three times the power of a common lithium iron phosphate battery.
The catch? Less energy per kilo than the best lithium cells. Changan's first sodium car is rated about four hundred kilometers, on China's generous test.
Would you trade range for a battery that shrugs off winter? Tell me below. Follow EV Drive.
